title: Elevation engagement architectures - dedicated to private migrations and SLA uplifts
body:
PURPOSE
This is a working blueprint for senior CS and AE teams to run elevation campaigns that move mid-market customers from hosted usage -> Dedicated capacity -> Private deployment (and/or add premium SLAs). The doc mixes a QBR-friendly one-pager, a renewal/health tracker snapshot format, outreach cadences, technical gating matrix, and sample messaging.

INTENDED USE CASES
- Quarterly QBR prep: distill tech & commercial posture into 1 slide + 1 pager ask
- Renewal window play: 6-18 months before renewal, surface cost/latency economics
- Migration pilot: define success criteria for Dedicated trial -> Private POC
- SLA upsell: identify when to offer 99.95/99.9 SLA, response targets, and premium pricing band

HIGH-LEVEL STRATEGY (elevation paths)
1) Cost-driven path (most common): customer pays primarily hosted; high token volume and rising spend trigger proposal for Dedicated commit to reduce unit cost.
2) Performance-driven path: latency-sensitive apps (avg p99 > target) -> recommend Dedicated with pinned model, autoscaling policy.
3) Compliance-driven path: regulated PII/PHI -> Private deployment + KMS/HSM, audit logging, SOC2/ISO artifacts for buy-in.
4) Risk mitigation path: customers with business-critical Uptime needs -> SLA uplift plus fallback model routing to cross-region Dedicated pools.

ONE-PAGE QBR FRAME (slide-friendly)
- Quick health: active routes, avg daily tokens, p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost per 1M tokens (hosted)
- Trend: 3mo token growth %, peak concurrency events, cache hit rate
- Pain point snapshot: top 3 technical & top 3 business blockers (e.g., inference cost, latency spikes, auditability)
- Suggested elevation: path + estimated monthly savings or cost change, recommended pilot size (GPU-hours or reserved vCPUs), timeline (pilot -> rollout)
- Ask: specific contract action (e.g., 6mo Dedicated trial at 30% discount, add 99.9 SLA for $X/mo)

RENEWAL / HEALTH TRACKER SNIPPET (QBR-ready table rows)
- Account: ACME Fintech
- CSM: Aisha P.
- ARR footprint: $120k hosted run-rate
- Signals: 42% MoM token growth; 7 incidents last 90d (most from infra cold-start)
- Recommended action: Dedicated 3-month pilot (16-GPU pool equivalent), SLA pilot 99.5 with 1h on-call during business hours
- Success metrics: -20% cost per token; p99 latency < 350ms 95% of the time; cache hit >= 25%

TECHNICAL GATING MATRIX (for moving to Dedicated / Private)
- Minimum signal thresholds: sustained 30% MoM growth OR run-rate > $50k/mo OR p99 latency > target or regulatory requirement flagged.
- Security gating: completed SOC2 docs review, customer admin access control audit, KMS integration feasibility call.
- Ops gating: monitoring hooks (console webhook + Datadog integration), rollback plan, model pinning and version policies.
- Integration checklist (for Private POC): VPC peering details, egress rules, cert exchange, test dataset for evals, perf baseline run.

PILOT DESIGN PRINCIPLES
- Narrow scope: start with 1–2 routes that account for >60% of tokens or are highest-value features.
- Timeboxed: 4–8 weeks pilot with pre-agreed SLOs and acceptance criteria.
- Measurable: baseline metrics captured for comparison, clear telemetry (token-level, per-route latency, kv-cache hit).
- Risk control: automatic fallback to hosted for any non-conforming traffic; billing cap and burn rate alerts.

ENGAGEMENT CADENCE (sample)
- Day 0: kickoff (30–60m) — technical owners + procurement intro.
- Week 1: integration checkpoints — perf baseline run + smoking tests.
- Week 2–3: optimization sprints — quantization/ batching suggestions from Optimize team, cache rules tuning.
- Week 4: business review — cost/latency delta, customer feedback, decide go/no-go.
- Week 6–8: rollout plan for production (if accepted) + contract amendment draft.

COMMERCIAL FRAMEWORK (pricing knobs)
- Trial pricing: 30–50% off committed price for pilots under 3 months; usage cap optional.
- Conversion: sliding scale discount based on annual commit size. Example: 10% off for $X/mo, 20% off for $2X/mo.
- SLA add-on: fixed monthly fee per account (tiered by concurrency band) + credits for downtime beyond target.

SAMPLE OUTREACH SEQUENCE (email/Slack templates)
- Initial business outreach subject: "Proposal: Reduce inference cost by ~25% for [Product/Route]"
  Body (short): "Hey [Name], we tracked increased token spend on [route]. We can run a 6-week Dedicated pilot to validate a 20–30% unit cost reduction while holding latency targets. Pilot is low-friction; our team manages the migration and fallbacks. Can we align next Wed?"
- Technical ping (after business interest): "Quick sync to confirm test dataset and VPC connectivity — would you share an engineer who can pair Thursday?"
- QBR slide blurb (one-liner): "Recommend Dedicated pilot to optimize unit economics; SLA uplift contingent on production rollout and monitoring hooks."

SAMPLE CONTRACT LANGUAGE (short)
- Pilot addendum: "Customer will receive a non-exclusive Dedicated pilot for a 60-day period. Usage beyond agreed cap billed at standard committed rates. Pilot includes up to two change windows per week and a single rollback plan. If customer converts to a Dedicated annual commitment within 30 days of pilot completion, Redwood will apply a conversion credit of $X."

RISKS AND MITIGATIONS
- Risk: Pilot fails to show cost delta because of small batch sizes. Mitigation: ensure test routes mirror production distribution; suggest synthetic load tests.
- Risk: Security review stalls Private conversion. Mitigation: prepackage SOC2 artifacts, templated network configs, and create a fast-track to Security review with prioritized SSO/KMS checklist.
- Risk: Unexpected latency due to model loading. Mitigation: KV cache tuning + warmed instance pool during pilot.

MEASURABLE OUTCOMES (for QBR follow-up)
- Commercial: committed ARR from conversion, pilot to conversion rate, average contract uplift %
- Technical: % reduction in cost/token, p95/p99 latency improvements, incidents reduced per quarter

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- What threshold should trigger AE outreach vs. CSM owning the conversation? Current draft: >$100k ARR -> AE involvement. Need feedback from revenue ops.
- Need templated legal language for cross-region data residency in Private contracts. Talk to Legal (Jemma).
- Capture a small set of customer case studies (2) to include in sales-ops pack.

NEXT ACTIONS / OWNER TAGS
- Build pilot pricing sketch (Miguel) - due 2025-12-05
- Draft technical runbook for pilot handoff (Jordan) - due 2026-01-10
- Validate threshold rules with RevOps (Leah) - due 2025-12-18

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLIST (copyable)
- [ ] Stakeholder alignment (CSM, AE, Eng owner)
- [ ] Baseline telemetry gathered (tokens, latency, errors)
- [ ] Security artifacts shared (SOC2, KMS notes)
- [ ] Pilot scope + timebox agreed
- [ ] Success metrics and go/no-go criteria written
- [ ] Contract addendum draft ready

---
Draft status: experimental. Pull this into QBR slide decks as the "elevation ask" 1-pager, and iterate after 2 live pilots.

References & links (internal): Confluence runbook (CONFL-2148), pilot pricing model (JIRA-7891), Optimize recommendations PR (github link in header).
